title: Time's Barbed Arrow: Irreversibility, Crypticity, and Stored Information
version: arXiv:0902.1209v1, 7 February 2009, 4 pages; published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 103, 094101 (published text not compared)
locator: p.2 left column (h_mu^- = h_mu^+ and symmetry of E); Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 (pp.2-3); definition of causal irreversibility Xi and crypticity (p.3)
assumptions: Stationary stochastic processes over a measurement alphabet; causal states from the epsilon-machine construction.
conclusion: Authors' claims: a stationary process is equally predictable in either scan direction; excess entropy E = I[past; future] = I[S^-; S^+]; C_mu^+ = E + H[S^+|S^-], C_mu^- = E + H[S^-|S^+]; causal irreversibility Xi = C_mu^+ - C_mu^- = H[S^+|S^-] - H[S^-|S^+].
proof_status: Letter format; Theorem 1 stated with an information-diagram argument, proofs deferred to references. Not re-derived here.
relevance: Prior art for Proposition 7 of the fixing note and statement S2 of the clock-content contract. Supplies an asymmetry (causal irreversibility) that the grade classification omits.
open_questions: Whether causal irreversibility gives a fourth grade or cuts across the three.
limits: Read through a page-extraction tool; equations partly garbled by extraction and reconstructed from context.

title: Time and Chance, chapter 6: The Asymmetries of Knowledge and Intervention
version: Harvard University Press, 2000; local PDF, text extracted with the system PDF library; printed pp. 116-130 (PDF pp. 131-145)
locator: p. 116 (prediction, retrodiction, records); pp. 117-119 (ready conditions and the past hypothesis); pp. 121-122 n. 11 (equal degree of constraint under Liouville); p. 122 (the two conditionalization procedures); pp. 125-130 (intervention and causal handles)
assumptions: Classical deterministic dynamics, the standard statistical rule, a past hypothesis.
conclusion: Author's claims: knowledge of the past beyond retrodiction rests on records, which need a past hypothesis; under determinism and Liouville, constraints at one time constrain every other time to the same degree, differing in form; the future counterfactually depends on what we control and the past does not.
dependencies: Chapters 4 and 5 of the same book, not reread.
relevance: Prior statement of reciprocity with zero imbalance for deterministic measure-preserving dynamics.
open_questions: Whether Albert anywhere compares regions that carry unequal information.
limits: First three pages of the chapter (pp. 113-115) not read. Extraction drops some ligatures.

title: Time's Arrow and Archimedes' Point
version: Oxford University Press, 1996 (local file dated 1997); printed pp. 145-146, 168-170, 259-260 only
locator: p. 146 (fixity of the past as conventional); pp. 168-170 (inputs fixed, outputs open, from the agent's perspective); pp. 259-260 (physics' concepts embody an open future)
assumptions: Author's perspectival account of causal asymmetry.
conclusion: Author's claim: the difference between the fixity of the past and the openness of the future is a feature of the agent's perspective, objective relative to our orientation.
dependencies: Chapters 6-7 as a whole, not read through.
relevance: Nearest philosophical predecessor for locating the fixed-open asymmetry outside the laws.
open_questions: Whether his treatment of the Gold universe contains a two-sided openness statement.
limits: Three short passages located by keyword search. The rest of the book was not read.

title: Information Symmetries in Irreversible Processes
relevance: Companion to Time's Barbed Arrow. Stationary discrete processes; time-asymmetric causal structure with time-symmetric information rate.
limits: Pages 1-3, 9, 11, 23, 25, 29 of about 30 read through a page extraction; labelled abstract depth because the central sections were not read.
